name: PLOD1
summary: PLOD1 encodes lysyl hydroxylase 1, an enzyme needed for the cross-links that give collagen its strength. One missense change, c.2032G>A (p.Gly678Arg), impairs it. Two copies cause fragile foal syndrome type 1, formerly Warmblood fragile foal syndrome: a foal with fragile, tearing skin and lax joints that is stillborn or cannot survive. It is recessive, and carriers have no known health problem. The allele is commonest in Warmbloods, where about 11 per cent of horses tested are carriers and it was found in 17 of 19 breeds; it is rare in Thoroughbreds, has been found in Knabstruppers, Haflingers and American Sport Ponies, and was not found in 302 Arabians. It was not associated with catastrophic breakdown in Thoroughbreds. No effect on coat, height, speed or build is established.

phenotypes.name: Wild type
phenotypes.description: Two working copies. Nothing is wrong and nothing is passed on.

phenotypes.name: PLOD1 carrier
phenotypes.description: One copy. No known clinical signs or health problems; the horse passes the copy to half its foals. A foal is affected only when both parents pass it on.

phenotypes.name: Fragile foal syndrome
phenotypes.description: Two copies. A collagen defect present from birth: thin, fragile, over-stretchy skin and mucous membranes that tear into open wounds from friction or pressure, sometimes before birth; over-extensible leg joints; floppy ears; and swellings of blood or fluid. Foals are often premature, and are stillborn, not viable, or put down shortly after birth. There is no treatment. Affected foals are typically carried to birth; that such pregnancies are routinely lost early has not been shown.
